definition_en: a very small living thing that can cause disease, or the first seed of an idea
core_image: 显微镜下一群微小的细菌在游动
scene: 用肥皂洗手能冲走细菌。Washing hands with soap removes germs.
sceneCN: 这里 germ 是「细菌；病菌」（第 1 个义项）；句意：用肥皂洗手能冲走细菌。

senses.title: Tiny living cause
senses.definition: a very small living thing, especially one that causes disease
senses.definitionCN: 极小的生物，尤指引起疾病的微生物
senses.example: Washing hands with soap removes germs.
senses.exampleCN: 用肥皂洗手能冲走细菌。
senses.why: The seed sense was borrowed for unseen living particles.
senses.whyCN: 「种子」的含义被借用来指看不见的活微粒。

senses.title: First seed of an idea
senses.definition: the first small beginning of an idea or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 想法或感情最初微小的开端
senses.example: There was a germ of truth in his story.
senses.exampleCN: 他的故事里有一点真实的萌芽。
senses.why: An idea starts as small as a seed.
senses.whyCN: 一个想法开始的时候，小得像一粒种子。

senses.title: Sprouting part
senses.definition: the part of a seed that can grow into a new plant
senses.definitionCN: 种子中能长成新植株的部分
senses.example: Wheat germ is rich in nutrients.
senses.exampleCN: 小麦胚芽富含营养。
senses.why: This is the oldest and most literal sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最古老也最字面的含义。

intro.en: Germ first meant a sprout and was later applied to microbes.
intro.cn: germ 最初指幼芽，后来被用来指微生物。

items.en: Germen meant a sprout, bud, or seed.
items.cn: germen 意为幼芽、芽或种子。

items.en: The word passed into French as germe.
items.cn: 这个词以 germe 的形式进入法语。

items.en: English used germ for the seed of a plant.
items.cn: 英语用 germ 指植物的种子。

items.en: It came to mean the beginning of an idea.
items.cn: 它逐渐指一个想法的开端。

items.en: The nineteenth century applied it to disease microbes.
items.cn: 十九世纪把它用于致病的微生物。

note.en: Germ is compared with look-alike words and words for tiny life and beginnings.
note.cn: 把 germ 与形近词以及表示微小生命和开端的词作比较。

the small part a plant grows from

normalIntro.en: A germ is a seed so small that only a microscope can find it.
normalIntro.cn: germ 是一粒小到只有显微镜才能找到的种子。

normal.en: Washing hands with soap removes germs.
normal.cn: 用肥皂洗手能冲走细菌。

normal.en: There was a germ of truth in his story.
normal.cn: 他的故事里有一点真实的萌芽。

normal.en: Wheat germ is rich in nutrients.
normal.cn: 小麦胚芽富含营养。

normal.en: Coughing can spread germs in a crowded room.
normal.cn: 咳嗽会在拥挤的房间里传播细菌。

normal.en: The germ of the plan came from a walk.
normal.cn: 这个计划的萌芽来自一次散步。

abstract.en: Every great idea begins as a germ no one else can see.
abstract.cn: 每一个伟大的想法，开始时都是一粒别人看不见的萌芽。

abstract.en: Small causes are still causes.
abstract.cn: 微小的原因仍然是原因。

abstract.en: A seed does not announce the tree.
abstract.cn: 种子从不预告它将长成的树。

examples.cn: 用肥皂洗手能冲走细菌。

dict_mnemonic.text: germ 原本是「幼芽、种子」：疾病的「种子」就是病菌，想法的「种子」就是萌芽；germ theory 是「病菌学说」，a germ of 是「一点……的萌芽」。

root: 来自拉丁语 germen（幼芽、种子），经古法语 germe 进入英语，核心义「能长成新东西的小种子」。

sensesIntro.en: Germ means a disease-causing microbe, the first small beginning of an idea, or the sprouting part of a seed.
sensesIntro.cn: germ 意为致病的微生物、想法最初的开端，或种子的胚芽。

core.en: A tiny seed from which something grows.
core.cn: 一粒能长出东西的微小种子。

branches.en: Under a lens, tiny shapes swim in a drop.
branches.cn: 在镜头下，一滴水里游动着微小的形状。

branches.en: One small doubt sits at the edge of a plan.
branches.cn: 一点小小的怀疑停在计划的边缘。

branches.en: A green tip pushes out of the soil.
branches.cn: 一个绿色的尖端从土里探出来。

branches.en: Both the microbe and the sprout begin invisibly small.
branches.cn: 微生物和幼芽开始时都小得看不见。

branches.en: An idea and a plant both grow from a hidden start.
branches.cn: 想法和植物都从隐蔽的起点生长。

intro.en: Germ has a family of sprouting, seed, and killing words.
intro.cn: germ 有一个由发芽、种子与杀灭组成的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin germen meant a sprout or bud.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 germen 意为幼芽或芽。

items.meaning: a microbe or a first seed
items.example: A germ can make you ill.

items.meaning: relating to a bud or early stage
items.exampleCN: 这个想法还处在萌芽阶段。
这种清洁剂含杀菌成分。

latinEntries.example: Germen is the source of germ.
latinEntries.exampleCN: germen 是 germ 的来源。
germinare 孕育了英语的 germinate。

definition_en: to begin to grow from a seed or spore, or to make such a thing begin to grow
core_image: 一粒豆子在湿纸巾里撑开种皮，白色的小根向下探
scene: 厨房里，一把湿纸巾裹着几粒豆子，放在温暖的窗边。 After five days in damp paper, the beans germinate and push a pale root out of their coats.
sceneCN: 这里 germinate 指「发芽」（第 1 个义项：种子开始长出幼根）；句意为在湿纸里放了五天后，豆子发芽，把白色的根顶出种皮。

senses.title: A seed begins to grow
senses.definition: of a seed, to break out of its coat and start growing
senses.definitionCN: 指种子突破种皮并开始生长
senses.example: The beans germinate in about five days.
senses.exampleCN: 豆子约五天发芽。
senses.why: the verb is intransitive here: the seed is the one that crosses the threshold, with no outside hand.
senses.whyCN: 这里动词是不及物的：跨过门槛的是种子自己，没有外来的手。

senses.title: Make seeds sprout on purpose
senses.definition: to cause seeds to begin growing before they are planted
senses.definitionCN: 在播种之前使种子开始生长
senses.example: Soak the peas and germinate them on a tray.
senses.exampleCN: 把豌豆泡水，然后在托盘上催芽。
senses.why: the transitive use adds an agent who controls the conditions, so the same verb takes a gardener as subject.
senses.whyCN: 及物用法增加了一个控制条件的施动者，因此同一个动词可以以园丁为主语。

senses.title: Sprout grain for malting
senses.definition: to start the growth of barley or other grain so that its starch changes
senses.definitionCN: 使大麦等谷物开始生长，从而改变其中的淀粉
senses.example: Maltsters germinate the barley for four days.
senses.exampleCN: 制麦师让大麦发芽四天。
senses.why: controlled sprouting is a manufacturing step, so the verb enters industry unchanged.
senses.whyCN: 受控发芽是一道制造工序，动词因此原样进入工业。

senses.title: A spore begins to grow
senses.definition: of a fungal or fern spore, to produce a first growth tube
senses.definitionCN: 指真菌或蕨的孢子长出第一根生长管
senses.example: The spores germinate only on a wet surface.
senses.exampleCN: 这些孢子只在湿润表面萌发。
senses.why: spores repeat the seed's gesture, so the botanical verb extends to them without a new word.
senses.whyCN: 孢子重复种子的动作，因此植物学动词不加新词便延伸到它们。

senses.title: A pollen grain grows a tube
senses.definition: of a pollen grain, to produce a tube after landing on a compatible stigma
senses.definitionCN: 指花粉粒落在亲和柱头后长出花粉管
senses.example: The pollen grains germinate within hours of landing.
senses.exampleCN: 花粉粒落地数小时内就萌发。
senses.why: the tube is the grain's root, so the verb keeps its literal growing sense inside a flower.
senses.whyCN: 花粉管就是花粉粒的根，因此动词在花内仍保留字面的生长义。

senses.title: Metaphor: an idea starts to develop
senses.definition: figurative, of a plan or feeling, to begin to develop from a small beginning
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指计划或情感从小处开始发展
senses.example: The idea germinated while she was walking home.
senses.exampleCN: 这个想法在她走路回家时萌生了。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the threshold and the hidden start, so nothing is visible until it breaks out.
senses.whyCN: 比喻保留了门槛与隐蔽的起点，因此在破壳之前什么也看不见。

senses.title: Sprout under the right conditions
senses.definition: to begin growth when warmth, moisture and air allow it
senses.definitionCN: 在温度、水分与空气允许时开始生长
senses.example: These seeds germinate only when the soil reaches fifteen degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 这些种子只有在土温达到十五度时才发芽。
senses.why: conditions are the gate, so the verb often appears with an only-when clause.
senses.whyCN: 条件是闸门，因此这个动词常与「只有……才」从句连用。

senses.title: Chit seed potatoes before planting
senses.definition: to encourage short shoots on tubers before they go into the ground
senses.definitionCN: 在入土之前促使块茎长出短芽
senses.example: Gardeners germinate their seed potatoes in a cool, bright shed.
senses.exampleCN: 园丁在阴凉明亮的棚里给种薯催芽。
senses.why: a tuber is not a seed but behaves like one at planting time, so the verb follows the practical resemblance.
senses.whyCN: 块茎不是种子，但在播种时表现得像种子，动词于是跟着实际相似性走。

intro.en: Germinate comes from Latin germinare 'to sprout', from germen 'sprout, bud, seed'. The deeper origin of germen is uncertain. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: germinate 来自拉丁 germinare「发芽」，后者出自 germen「芽、胚、种子」。germen 的更早来源不确定。年代均为约数。

items.en: Germen named a sprout or bud, the living point from which a plant extends.
items.cn: germen 指芽或幼枝，即植物向外伸展的那个活的起点。

items.en: Source uncertain: the ancestry of germen before Latin is not settled; a link to a root meaning 'produce, beget' is a reconstruction, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: 来源不确定：germen 在拉丁语之前的谱系没有定论；把它连到意为「产生、生育」的词根属于重构，而非已证实的派生。

items.en: Germinare 'to sprout' is a first-conjugation verb built on germen; its noun is germinatio.
items.cn: germinare「发芽」是建立在 germen 上的第一变位动词；其名词为 germinatio。

items.en: English germinate appears in the seventeenth century, first of plants and later of spores and pollen.
items.cn: 英语 germinate 于 17 世纪出现，先指植物，后指孢子与花粉。

items.en: Malting gave the verb a manufacturing sense, since controlled sprouting is how barley starch is made available.
items.cn: 制麦给了这个动词工业义，因为受控发芽正是让大麦淀粉变得可用的方式。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the earliest printed use of germinate is not firmly established; the seventeenth-century placement is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：germinate 最早见于印刷的时间没有确证；归于 17 世纪只是约数。

note.en: Group one separates the germ- family by word class and spelling; group two separates sprouting from the stages before and after it.
note.cn: 第一组按词类与拼写区分 germ- 词族；第二组区分发芽与其前后阶段。

entries.definition: The process the verb names; the verb says what happens, the noun says what it is called.
entries.definitionCN: 动词所指的过程；动词说发生了什么，名词说它叫什么。

entries.definition: The embryo or a microbe; the verb needs a germ to act on, but the germ is not the action.
entries.definitionCN: 胚或微生物；动词需要有胚才能作用，但胚不是动作。

entries.definition: Relating to an early stage; it describes where something is, not that it is sprouting.
entries.definitionCN: 与早期阶段有关；描述事物所处的位置，而非它正在发芽。

entries.definition: From Latin germanus 'closely related', not germen; it means relevant, and the resemblance is accidental.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 germanus「近亲的」，并非 germen；意为相关，相似纯属巧合。

entries.definition: The common verb for a shoot appearing; germinate is its technical counterpart, used in labs and seed testing.
entries.definitionCN: 嫩芽出现的日常动词；germinate 是它在实验室与种子检验中的术语对应词。

entries.definition: To form a bud, the small swelling that will become a shoot or flower; buds form after germination, not during it.
entries.definitionCN: 形成芽，即日后长成枝条或花的小突起；芽在发芽之后形成，而不在发芽之中。

entries.definition: To join gametes or feed soil; in a flower it happens before the seed can germinate.
entries.definitionCN: 使配子结合或给土壤施肥；在花中它发生在种子能够发芽之前。

entries.definition: To keep eggs or cultures at the right warmth so that development can proceed; it names the care, not the emergence.
entries.definitionCN: 把卵或培养物保持在合适温度，使发育得以进行；它指照料，而非破出。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real root, the real agricultural phrases and the real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的词根、真实的农事搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: germen 'sprout' + -ate: to do the sprout thing.
normal.cn: germen「芽」+ -ate：做「发芽」这件事。

normal.en: The same root gives germ, germinal, germination.
normal.cn: 同一词根衍生 germ、germinal、germination。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: germinate seeds, germinate barley, germinate quickly.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：催芽、使大麦发芽、很快发芽。

normal.en: Water, warmth and air are the three gates the verb waits behind.
normal.cn: 水、温度与空气是这个动词所等待的三道闸门。

normal.en: Both seeds and spores take the same verb.
normal.cn: 种子与孢子都接受同一个动词。

abstract.en: Picture a parcel splitting at one seam and a small root slipping out.
abstract.cn: 想象一个包裹沿一条缝裂开，一小段根滑了出来。

abstract.en: Picture a bare field that shows green only after the third warm day.
abstract.cn: 想象一片裸地，只在第三个暖日之后才露绿。

abstract.en: Picture a remark that stays quiet for months and then becomes a plan.
abstract.cn: 想象一句话安静了几个月，然后变成一项计划。

examples.en: The seeds germinate within a week if kept moist.
examples.cn: 保持湿润的话，这些种子一周内发芽。

examples.en: Farmers germinate barley before it goes to the malt floor.
examples.cn: 农民在把大麦送去制麦之前先让它发芽。

examples.en: The idea germinated during a long walk.
examples.cn: 这个想法在一次长距离散步中萌生。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「germ（芽）+ inate」——让芽从种皮里出来 → 发芽

root: 拉丁 germen, germinis「芽、胚、种子」→ germinare「发芽」→ 英语 germinate。germen 更早来源不确定，与「产生、生育」词根的联系属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of germinate all cross one threshold: something enclosed starts to grow, whether the grower is nature, a gardener, a maltster or a laboratory.
sensesIntro.cn: germinate 的八个义项都跨过同一个门槛：封闭之物开始生长，无论促成者是自然、园丁、制麦师还是实验室。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a coat splits and a root reaches down.
core.cn: 核心意象：种皮裂开，一支根向下探。

branches.en: NATURAL START: the seed does it itself once the conditions allow.
branches.cn: 自然开始：条件许可时，种子自己完成。

branches.en: HUMAN START: a gardener can force the same event on a tray or a tuber.
branches.cn: 人为开始：园丁能在托盘或块茎上促成同样的事件。

branches.en: INDUSTRIAL START: controlled sprouting makes grain starch usable.
branches.cn: 工业开始：受控发芽使谷物淀粉变得可用。

branches.en: OTHER GRAINS: spores and pollen repeat the gesture at a smaller scale.
branches.cn: 其他颗粒：孢子与花粉在更小尺度上重复同一动作。

branches.en: METAPHOR: a plan crosses the same threshold quietly.
branches.cn: 比喻：计划同样安静地跨过这一门槛。

intro.en: Germinate is a Latin noun turned into a verb, and the same base yields the embryo, the act and the capacity.
intro.cn: germinate 是拉丁名词转成的动词，同一词基衍生出胚、动作与能力。

latinIntro.en: Latin germen 'sprout' gives germinare; English builds germ, germinate, germination and germinal from the same stock.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 germen「芽」衍生 germinare；英语在同一词族上构成 germ、germinate、germination 与 germinal。

items.example: Germen names the point of new growth.
Germinate means to perform the sprouting.

items.meaning: tending to, having the power to
items.exampleCN: 有发芽力的种子容易发芽。

items.example: Each germ holds a tiny plant.
items.exampleCN: 每个胚里都藏着一株小小的植物。

items.meaning: of a germ or an early stage

items.exampleCN: 长期贮藏会使发芽能力下降。

definition_en: a movement of the body that expresses meaning, or a symbolic act
core_image: 一个人抬手向门口一指，示意客人先走
scene: 他朝门口做了个手势。He made a gesture towards the door.
sceneCN: 这里 gesture 是「手势」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他朝门口做了个手势。

senses.title: Movement of the body
senses.definition: a movement of the hands or body that shows meaning
senses.definitionCN: 手或身体的、表达含义的动作
senses.example: He made a gesture towards the door.
senses.exampleCN: 他朝门口做了个手势。
senses.why: The Latin source names the carrying of the body, then a movement of it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源先指身体的姿态，后指身体的动作。

senses.title: Symbolic act
senses.definition: an action that expresses an attitude or feeling
senses.definitionCN: 表达某种态度或感情的行为
senses.example: Sending flowers was a nice gesture.
senses.exampleCN: 送花是个善意的表示。
senses.why: A small act can carry a message as clearly as a hand does.
senses.whyCN: 一个小举动可以像手势一样清楚地传递信息。

senses.title: To signal with the body
senses.definition: to move the hands or body to express or direct something
senses.definitionCN: 移动手或身体来表达或指示某事
senses.example: She gestured for us to sit down.
senses.exampleCN: 她示意我们坐下。
senses.why: The noun became a verb naming the act of making a sign.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化成了动词，表示做出示意的动作。

intro.en: Gesture comes from Latin words for carrying and bearing the body.
intro.cn: gesture 来自拉丁语中表示承载和身体姿态的词。

items.en: Gerere meant to carry or perform.
items.cn: gerere 意为承载或施行。

items.en: Gestus meant a bearing or movement of the body.
items.cn: gestus 意为身体的姿态或动作。

items.en: Gestura named the making of such movements.
items.cn: gestura 指做出这类动作。

items.en: English used gesture for expressive body movement.
items.cn: 英语用 gesture 指富有表现力的身体动作。

items.en: It widened to symbolic acts and then to a verb.
items.cn: 它的含义扩展到象征性举动，后来又变成动词。

note.en: Gesture is compared with look-alike words and words for signs and movements.
note.cn: 把 gesture 与形近词以及表示信号和动作的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: A gesture is a sentence spoken with the body.
normalIntro.cn: gesture 是用身体说出的句子。

normal.en: He made a gesture towards the door.
normal.cn: 他朝门口做了个手势。

normal.en: Sending flowers was a nice gesture.
normal.cn: 送花是个善意的表示。

normal.en: She gestured for us to sit down.
normal.cn: 她示意我们坐下。

normal.en: He spoke with wide hand gestures.
normal.cn: 他说话时手比划得很大。

normal.en: A small gesture can mean a great deal.
normal.cn: 一个小小的举动可以意义重大。

abstract.en: Some messages are carried better by hands than by words.
abstract.cn: 有些信息用手传达比用词更好。

abstract.en: A gesture is a promise made visible.
abstract.cn: 姿态是一个看得见的承诺。

abstract.en: What the body says, the mouth often repeats.
abstract.cn: 身体说过的话，嘴常常再说一遍。

examples.en: He made a gesture towards the door.
examples.cn: 他朝门口做了个手势。

examples.en: Sending flowers was a nice gesture.
examples.cn: 送花是个善意的表示。

examples.cn: 她示意我们坐下。

dict_mnemonic.text: gesture 与 suggest、digest 共享拉丁词根 gerere（承载、施展）：身体「施展」出来的动作就是手势；make a gesture 是「做手势」，a gesture of 是「……的表示」。

root: 来自拉丁语 gestus（身体的姿态、动作），由 gerere（承载、施行）而来，核心义「身体做出的示意动作」。

sensesIntro.en: Gesture means a meaningful body movement, a symbolic act, or to signal with the body.
sensesIntro.cn: gesture 意为富有含义的身体动作、象征性的举动，或用动作示意。

core.en: The body saying something without words.
core.cn: 身体不用词语地说出某事。

branches.en: A hand points the way to a door.
branches.cn: 一只手指出通向门口的方向。

branches.en: Flowers arrive with no card at all.
branches.cn: 花送到了，却一张卡片也没有。

branches.en: A host waves everyone to the table.
branches.cn: 主人挥手让大家入席。

branches.en: One moving hand both shows and tells.
branches.cn: 一只移动的手既展示又告知。

branches.en: A small act and a small sign carry the same warmth.
branches.cn: 小小的举动与小小的示意传递同样的温暖。

intro.en: Gesture belongs to a Latin family of carrying, bearing, and signaling.
intro.cn: gesture 属于拉丁语中表示承载、姿态与示意的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin gerere meant to carry or perform.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 gerere 意为承载或施行。

items.example: His gestures were easy to read.
He gestured to the empty chair.
She kept gesturing while she spoke.
items.exampleCN: 她说话时不停地打手势。

items.example: The painting has a gestural style.
items.exampleCN: 这幅画有一种手势化的风格。
她的手势吸引了所有人的目光。

items.meaning: to bring an idea to mind
items.example: The note suggests a change of plan.
items.exampleCN: 这张便条暗示计划有变。

latinEntries.example: Gestus is the source of gesture.
latinEntries.exampleCN: gestus 是 gesture 的来源。

latinEntries.example: Gerere lies behind gestus and suggest.
latinEntries.exampleCN: gerere 是 gestus 与 suggest 共同的源头。

definition_en: to obtain something, to become a certain way, to reach a place, or to understand
core_image: 一双手终于接到从空中抛来的钥匙
scene: 她终于得到了那份工作。She finally got the job she wanted.
sceneCN: 这里 get 是「得到；获得」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她终于得到了那份工作。

senses.title: Obtain
senses.definition: to receive or obtain something
senses.definitionCN: 接到或获得某物
senses.example: She finally got the job she wanted.
senses.exampleCN: 她终于得到了那份想要的工作。
senses.why: This is the oldest core sense: to come to have something.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的核心义：使某物来到自己手中。

senses.title: Become
senses.definition: to become or start to be in a certain state
senses.definitionCN: 变成或开始处于某种状态
senses.example: It gets cold here after sunset.
senses.exampleCN: 这里日落后会变冷。
senses.why: Coming to have a state is like coming to have a thing.
senses.whyCN: 「进入某种状态」就像「得到某样东西」。

senses.title: Reach
senses.definition: to arrive at a place or reach a point
senses.definitionCN: 到达某地或抵达某个位置
senses.example: We got home before the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在下雨前到了家。
senses.why: Arriving is obtaining a place with your body.
senses.whyCN: 抵达就是用身体「获得」一个位置。

senses.title: Understand
senses.definition: to understand something, especially a joke or idea
senses.definitionCN: 理解某事，尤指笑话或想法
senses.example: I get the point now.
senses.exampleCN: 我现在明白这个意思了。
senses.why: To get an idea is to take hold of it with the mind.
senses.whyCN: 「得到」一个想法，就是用头脑把它抓住。

intro.en: Get came from Old Norse and spread into many meanings in English.
intro.cn: get 来自古诺斯语，在英语中扩展出许多含义。

items.en: Geta meant to obtain or reach.
items.cn: geta 意为获得或到达。

items.en: The verb entered English as geten.
items.cn: 这个动词以 geten 进入英语。

items.en: It covered obtaining, seizing, and arriving.
items.cn: 它涵盖获得、抓取和到达。

items.en: It developed the sense of becoming.
items.cn: 它发展出「变得」的含义。

items.en: It also came to mean understanding.
items.cn: 它也开始表示理解。

note.en: Get is compared with look-alike words and verbs of obtaining.
note.cn: 把 get 与形近词以及表示获得的动词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Get is the everyday verb for coming to have something.
normalIntro.cn: get 是表示「得到某物」的日常动词。

normal.en: She finally got the job she wanted.
normal.cn: 她终于得到了那份想要的工作。

normal.en: It gets cold here after sunset.
normal.cn: 这里日落后会变冷。

normal.en: We got home before the rain.
normal.cn: 我们在下雨前到了家。

normal.en: I get the point now.
normal.cn: 我现在明白这个意思了。

normal.en: Let us get ready for the trip.
normal.cn: 我们为旅行做好准备吧。

abstract.en: To get is to close the distance between want and hand.
abstract.cn: 得到，就是缩短愿望与手之间的距离。

abstract.en: Some things are got by waiting, others by walking.
abstract.cn: 有些东西靠等待得到，有些靠走过去得到。

abstract.en: Understanding is getting an idea to stay.
abstract.cn: 理解，就是让一个想法留下来。

examples.en: She finally got the job she wanted.
examples.cn: 她终于得到了那份想要的工作。

examples.en: We got home before the rain.
examples.cn: 我们在下雨前到了家。

examples.en: I get the point now.
examples.cn: 我现在明白这个意思了。

dict_mnemonic.text: get 是英语里含义最广的动词之一：得到、变得、到达、理解都可用它；get ready 是「准备好」，get rid of 是「摆脱」，get to 是「到达」。

root: 来自古诺斯语 geta（获得、到达），进入英语后含义大幅扩展，核心义「使某物来到自己这里」。

sensesIntro.en: Get means to obtain, to become, to reach, or to understand.
sensesIntro.cn: get 意为得到、变得、到达或理解。

core.en: Bringing something into your possession or reach.
core.cn: 把某物带入自己的掌握或触及范围。

branches.en: A hand closes around a key.
branches.cn: 一只手合拢，握住一把钥匙。

branches.en: The evening air turns cool.
branches.cn: 傍晚的空气变凉了。

branches.en: A traveller steps through the front door.
branches.cn: 旅人走进了前门。

branches.en: A joke lands and the listener smiles.
branches.cn: 笑话奏效，听的人笑了。

branches.en: Holding a thing and holding an idea use the same verb.
branches.cn: 握住一个东西和抓住一个想法，用的是同一个动词。

intro.en: Get forms a small family of compounds and a few old related verbs.
intro.cn: get 构成一小族复合词和几个古老的同源动词。

latinIntro.en: Get has no Latin root; it came from Old Norse.
latinIntro.cn: get 没有拉丁词根，它来自古诺斯语。

items.exampleCN: 他得到了一辆新自行车。

items.example: They have gotten used to it.

items.meaning: an escape or a short holiday
items.exampleCN: 他们计划了一次周末短途出行。

definition_en: something given to someone without payment, or a natural ability
core_image: 一个包着彩纸的盒子被双手递到另一双手中
scene: 她给孩子买了一份生日礼物。She bought a birthday gift for the child.
sceneCN: 这里 gift 是「礼物」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她给孩子买了一份生日礼物。

senses.title: Something given
senses.definition: something given to someone without payment, often for a special occasion
senses.definitionCN: 无偿送给别人的东西，常在特殊场合赠送
senses.example: She bought a birthday gift for the child.
senses.exampleCN: 她给孩子买了一份生日礼物。
senses.why: The original sense is simply something handed over as a favour.
senses.whyCN: 最初的含义就是出于好意递给别人的东西。

senses.title: Natural ability
senses.definition: a natural ability that someone is born with
senses.definitionCN: 与生俱来的能力
senses.example: She has a gift for languages.
senses.exampleCN: 她有语言天赋。
senses.why: A talent was seen as something given by nature.
senses.whyCN: 天赋被看作是大自然赠予的东西。

senses.title: The act of giving
senses.definition: the act of giving something formally to another
senses.definitionCN: 正式把某物赠与他人的行为
senses.example: The land came to the town by gift.
senses.exampleCN: 这块土地是通过赠与归城镇所有的。
senses.why: The object and the act of handing it over share one word.
senses.whyCN: 所赠之物与赠予行为共用同一个词。

intro.en: Gift came from the Norse word for a present or favour.
intro.cn: gift 来自诺斯语中表示礼物或恩惠的词。

items.en: Gipt meant a gift or a piece of luck.
items.cn: gipt 意为礼物或好运。

items.en: Gift first named a dowry or marriage gift.
items.cn: gift 最初指嫁妆或婚姻赠礼。

items.en: It widened to any present.
items.cn: 它扩展为任何礼物。

items.en: It came to mean a natural ability.
items.cn: 它逐渐表示天赋。

items.en: The verb gift named the formal act of giving.
items.cn: 动词 gift 指正式的赠予行为。

note.en: Gift is compared with look-alike words and words for presents and abilities.
note.cn: 把 gift 与形近词以及表示礼物和能力词作比较。

entries.definition: money or goods given to a cause

normalIntro.en: A gift moves from one pair of hands to another with no price attached.
normalIntro.cn: gift 从一双手移到另一双手，却不带价格。

normal.en: She bought a birthday gift for the child.
normal.cn: 她给孩子买了一份生日礼物。

normal.en: She has a gift for languages.

normal.en: The free gift came with the magazine.
normal.cn: 这份赠品随杂志附送。

abstract.en: The best gift is the one the giver also needed.
abstract.cn: 最好的礼物，是送礼人自己也需要的那个。

abstract.en: Talent is a gift that still asks for practice.
abstract.cn: 天赋是一份仍然要求练习的礼物。

abstract.en: What is given with love arrives twice.
abstract.cn: 带着爱给出的东西，会到达两次。

root: 来自古诺斯语 gipt（礼物、好运），与 give 同源，核心义「无偿给予的东西」。

sensesIntro.en: Gift means something given without payment, a natural ability, or the act of giving.
sensesIntro.cn: gift 意为无偿赠送的东西、天赋，或赠与的行为。

core.en: Something handed over with no price.
core.cn: 不带价格地递出去的东西。

branches.en: A wrapped box passes across a table.
branches.cn: 一个包好的盒子从桌子一端递到另一端。

branches.en: A child plays a tune after hearing it once.
branches.cn: 孩子只听一遍就能把曲子弹出来。

branches.en: Land is handed to a town by agreement.
branches.cn: 土地依照协议被交给一座城镇。

branches.en: A present and a talent are both things received.
branches.cn: 礼物与天赋都是被接收的东西。

branches.en: Giving and being gifted share one idea of handing over.
branches.cn: 给予与有天赋共享「递出」这一个概念。

intro.en: Gift builds a family about presents, talents, and giving.
intro.cn: gift 构成一组关于礼物、天赋与给予的词。

latinIntro.en: Gift has no Latin root; it came from Old Norse gipt.
latinIntro.cn: gift 没有拉丁词根，它来自古诺斯语 gipt。

definition_en: a tall African animal with a long neck, or the brown-and-cream pattern of its coat
core_image: 动物园里长颈鹿伸长脖子够树梢的叶子
scene: 动物园里长颈鹿伸长脖子够树梢的叶子。The giraffe reached for leaves at the top of the tree.
sceneCN: 这里 giraffe 是「长颈鹿」（第 01 个义项）；句意是长颈鹿够到了树梢的叶子。

senses.title: A tall African animal with a long neck
senses.definition: a tall African animal with a long neck

senses.why: Giraffe came through Italian and French from Arabic zarafa, the name of this tall browsing animal.

senses.title: The brown-and-cream pattern of its coat
senses.definition: the brown-and-cream coat pattern of that animal
senses.definitionCN: 长颈鹿皮毛的棕白斑纹
senses.example: She wore a scarf with a giraffe print.
senses.exampleCN: 她戴了一条长颈鹿花纹的围巾。
senses.why: Textiles borrowed the animal's name for its coat pattern, as English also does with leopard print.
senses.whyCN: 纺织业借这种动物的名字来指它的皮毛花纹，英语对 leopard print 也这样做。

definition_en: to hand something to someone, to donate, or to yield
core_image: 双手把一件东西递到别人面前
scene: 请把盐递给我。Please give me the salt.
sceneCN: 这里 give 是「递给」（第 1 个义项）；句意：请把盐递给我。

senses.title: To hand something over
senses.definition: to hand something to someone so they can have it
senses.definitionCN: 把某物递到别人手里让对方持有
senses.example: Please give me the salt.
senses.exampleCN: 请把盐递给我。

senses.title: To donate
senses.definition: to hand something over without asking for payment
senses.definitionCN: 把东西交出去而不索取报酬

definition_zh: 冰川的；冰期的；极冷的；冷淡的；极缓慢的；冰状的
definition_en: relating to glaciers or ice, and hence extremely cold, unfriendly or slow
core_image: 一整片蓝白色的冰压在石头上，冰面冷得连空气都像静止
scene: 高原的夏天，湖面仍浮着碎冰，风吹过来像从冰库里放出来的。The wind off the glacial lake cut through their coats.
sceneCN: 这里 glacial 指「冰川的、来自冰川的」（第 1 个义项：与冰川或冰体有关的）；句意为冰川湖吹来的风穿透了他们的外套。

pos.zh: 冰川的；冰期的；极冷的；冷淡的；极缓慢的；（化学）冰状的

derivatives.zh: glaci-（拉丁 glacies「冰」）+ -er（法语 -ier，源自拉丁 -arium，表事物）→ 会流动的冰体：冰川
glaci-（拉丁 glacies「冰」）+ -ation（拉丁 -atio，表过程）→ 冰覆盖与流动的过程：冰川作用、冰期
glaci-（拉丁 glacies「冰」）+ -ate（拉丁 -atus，动词后缀）→ 使受冰川作用；使冻结
glacial + -ly（古英语 -lice，副词后缀）→ 以冰川的方式；引申为冷淡地、极慢地
glacio-（冰）+ -logy（希腊 -logia，表学科）→ 研究冰与冰川的学科：冰川学

senses.title: Of glaciers or ice
senses.titleCN: 冰川的：与冰川或冰体有关的
senses.definition: relating to a glacier or to ice formed by glacial action
senses.definitionCN: 与冰川或由冰川作用形成的冰有关的
senses.example: The wind off the glacial lake cut through their coats.
senses.exampleCN: 冰川湖吹来的风穿透了他们的外套。
senses.why: glacial is the adjective of glacies 'ice', so its first duty is simply to mark anything made of or fed by ice.
senses.whyCN: glacial 是 glacies「冰」的形容词，首要职责就是标记任何由冰构成或由冰供养的事物。

senses.title: Of an ice age
senses.titleCN: 冰期的：属于冰川时期的
senses.definition: belonging to a period when ice sheets covered large areas
senses.definitionCN: 属于冰盖覆盖大片陆地的时期
senses.example: Glacial periods alternate with warmer intervals.
senses.exampleCN: 冰期与较暖的间冰期交替出现。
senses.why: geology turns the adjective into a label for a whole stretch of time, because ice cover is its defining feature.
senses.whyCN: 地质学把这个形容词变成一整段时间的标签，因为冰盖正是那段时间的界定特征。

senses.title: Extremely cold
senses.definition: so cold that it feels like ice
senses.definitionCN: 冷得如同冰一样
senses.example: A glacial wind swept the empty square.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵冰冷的风扫过空荡的广场。
senses.why: the physical cold of ice is transferred directly to air and water, with no metaphor beyond the temperature itself.
senses.whyCN: 冰的物理寒冷被直接移到空气与水上，除了温度本身并无额外比喻。

senses.title: Cold in manner
senses.definition: unfriendly and emotionally distant in manner
senses.definitionCN: 态度不友好、情感疏远的
senses.example: She gave him a glacial stare and walked on.
senses.exampleCN: 她冷冷地看了他一眼，继续走开。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the temperature and moves it from air to feeling: a frozen manner chills the room.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了温度，只把它从空气移到情感：冰冷的态度让整个房间降温。

senses.title: Extremely slow
senses.definition: proceeding at a pace as slow as a glacier
senses.definitionCN: 以像冰川一样缓慢的速度推进
senses.example: Progress on the reform was glacial.
senses.exampleCN: 改革进展极其缓慢。
senses.why: glaciers move metres a year, so glacial becomes a standard measure of almost invisible speed.
senses.whyCN: 冰川一年只移动几米，因此 glacial 成为「几乎看不见的速度」的标准说法。

senses.title: Produced by glacial action
senses.titleCN: 冰川造成的：冰川沉积与地貌
senses.definition: formed or deposited by the action of a glacier
senses.definitionCN: 由冰川作用形成或沉积的
senses.example: Glacial deposits cover the plain north of the river.
senses.exampleCN: 冰川沉积覆盖着河以北的平原。
senses.why: in geology the adjective marks origin, not temperature: the material is glacial because a glacier put it there.
senses.whyCN: 在地质学中，这个形容词标记来源而非温度：材料之所以是 glacial，因为冰川把它放在那里。

senses.title: Ice-like in chemistry
senses.definition: of an acid so concentrated that it resembles ice
senses.definitionCN: 指浓到近乎冰状的酸
senses.example: Glacial acetic acid is almost pure acetic acid.
senses.exampleCN: 冰醋酸几乎是纯乙酸。
senses.why: the old chemical usage kept the literal image: the liquid is pure enough to freeze at room temperature and look like ice.
senses.whyCN: 古老的化学用法保留了字面意象：液体纯到能在室温凝固、看起来像冰。

senses.title: Carved by ice
senses.titleCN: 冰川刻蚀的：U 形谷与冰蚀地貌
senses.definition: shaped by the erosive passage of ice, as a valley or a rock surface
senses.definitionCN: 被冰的侵蚀通过所塑造，如谷地或岩面
senses.example: A glacial valley has steep sides and a broad floor.
senses.exampleCN: 冰川谷两侧陡峭、谷底宽阔。
senses.why: the valley shape is evidence of ice, so the adjective marks origin in the landform itself.
senses.whyCN: 山谷的形状就是冰的证据，因此这个形容词在景观本身中标记来源。

intro.en: Glacial comes from Latin glacialis 'icy', from glacies 'ice'. English borrowed it in the sixteenth century; the geological senses developed in the nineteenth. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: glacial 来自拉丁 glacialis「冰的」，出 glacies「冰」。英语于 16 世纪借入；地质学各义在 19 世纪发展出来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Glacies meant ice, whether on water or on a mountain. Its deeper root is reconstructed rather than attested.
items.cn: glacies 意为冰，无论水面之冰还是山中之冰。其更深词根属重构而非实证。

items.en: Glacialis 'icy, frozen' was formed with the adjective suffix -alis; Latin could apply it to water, wind, metal and human temperament.
items.cn: glacialis「冰的、冻结的」由形容词后缀 -alis 构成；拉丁语可用它形容水、风、金属与人的性情。

items.en: Sixteenth-century English uses glacial for icy cold; the spelling and meaning come through French and directly from Latin.
items.cn: 16 世纪英语用 glacial 表示「冰冷的」；拼写与词义经法语或直接取自拉丁语。

items.en: When glacial theory was accepted in the nineteenth century, glacial acquired its technical senses of ice ages, deposits and erosion.
items.cn: 19 世纪冰川学说被接受后，glacial 获得冰期、沉积与侵蚀等技术义。

items.en: Twentieth-century English extends glacial to manner (a glacial stare) and to speed (glacial progress), both keeping the core image of ice.
items.cn: 20 世纪英语把 glacial 扩展到态度（冷淡的一瞥）与速度（极慢的进展），两者都保留冰的核心意象。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin origin of glacies remains a reconstruction, and the first date of each transferred sense is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根存疑）：glacies 在拉丁语之前的来源仍属重构，各引申义的首见年代也只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound close but are not built on ice; group two holds the cold adjectives with which glacial is often confused.
note.cn: 第一组是形音相近却不以冰为词根的词；第二组是常与 glacial 混淆的寒冷形容词。

entries.definition: A worker who fits glass; its root is glass, so it has nothing to do with glaciers.
entries.definitionCN: 安装玻璃的工人；词根是 glass，与冰川无关。

entries.definition: A French word for iced or sugared fruit; the final accent and vowel separate it from glacial.
entries.definitionCN: 法语词，指糖渍或加冰的水果；重音与元音都与 glacial 不同。

entries.definition: A gentle artificial or natural slope; spelled almost like glacial but pronounced with a final s.
entries.definitionCN: 平缓的人工或天然斜坡；拼写近似 glacial，但末尾读作 s。

entries.definition: A grey-green bloom on leaves or fruit; only the opening sounds resemble glacial.
entries.definitionCN: 叶片或果实表面的灰绿色粉层；只有开头音近似 glacial。

entries.definition: Of the region around the North Pole; it names a place, while glacial names ice or coldness.
entries.definitionCN: 指北极附近地区；它命名地点，而 glacial 命名冰或寒冷。

entries.definition: Extremely cold, and in common use also meaning sexually uninterested.
entries.definitionCN: 极冷的，日常也指对性事毫无兴趣。

entries.definition: Covered with ice or as cold as ice; it is the everyday word that glacial formalizes.
entries.definitionCN: 覆冰的或冷如冰的；它是 glacial 所正式化的日常词。

entries.definition: Covered with frost, or unfriendly in manner; it concerns a thin surface, not a glacier.
entries.definitionCN: 覆霜的，或态度冷淡的；它涉及薄薄一层表面，而非冰川。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real suffixes, real relatives and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的后缀、同族词与固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: glacial = glaci- (ice) + -al (relating to): the adjective of ice in all its forms.
normal.cn: glacial = glaci-（冰）+ -al（与……有关）：冰在各种形态下的形容词。

normal.en: The same adjective covers cold air, a cold stare and a cold pace; the temperature image does all three jobs.
normal.cn: 同一个形容词覆盖冷空气、冷淡目光与缓慢速度；温度意象同时完成三件事。

normal.en: Glacial period and glacial lake are technical; glacial pace and glacial stare are metaphors.
normal.cn: glacial period 与 glacial lake 是专业说法；glacial pace 与 glacial stare 是比喻。

normal.en: Glacial acetic acid is named for its ice-like appearance, not for a glacier.
normal.cn: 冰醋酸的名称来自它像冰的外观，而非冰川。

normal.en: Glacier is the noun, glacial is the adjective, glaciation is the event: one stem, three jobs.
normal.cn: glacier 是名词，glacial 是形容词，glaciation 是事件：一个词干，三种职能。

abstract.en: A glacial silence is a silence with a temperature.
abstract.cn: 冰川般的沉默是有温度的沉默。

abstract.en: Bureaucracies can move at a glacial pace and still reshape a country over a century.
abstract.cn: 官僚机构能以冰川般的速度前进，却仍在一个世纪里重塑一个国家。

abstract.en: The glacial past is still in the soil, in the shape of every valley.
abstract.cn: 冰川的过去仍留在土壤里，也留在每一道山谷的形状里。

examples.en: Glacial ice looks blue where it is compressed.
examples.cn: 冰川冰在受挤压处呈蓝色。

examples.en: The glacial period ended about ten thousand years ago.
examples.cn: 冰期在约一万年前结束。

examples.en: His glacial reply ended the conversation.
examples.cn: 他冷冰冰的回答结束了谈话。

dict_mnemonic.text: glaci（冰）+ -al（与……有关）：冰的、冰川的；温度引申为极冷与冷淡，速度引申为极慢，化学里则是像冰一样纯。

root: 拉丁 glacialis「冰的」，出 glacies「冰」；与 glacier、glaciation、glaciology 同族。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of glacial. One adjective follows ice wherever it goes: into a glacier, into an ice age, into cold air, into a cold manner, into a slow pace, into chemistry and into the land ice carved.
sensesIntro.cn: glacial 的八个义项。同一个形容词跟着冰走遍各处：进冰川、进冰期、进冷空气、进冷淡态度、进缓慢速度、进化学，最后进入冰刻出的土地。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: blue-white ice pressed against stone, cold enough to make the air seem still.
core.cn: 核心意象：蓝白色的冰压在石头上，冷得让空气都像静止。

branches.en: THE WORK OF ICE: the glacier itself, the deposits it leaves, the valleys it cuts.
branches.cn: 冰的工作：冰川本身、留下的沉积、刻出的谷地。

branches.en: ICE AS TIME: a whole period named by its cover.
branches.cn: 冰作为时间：以冰盖命名的一整段时期。

branches.en: ICE AS TEMPERATURE: the literal cold of air and water.
branches.cn: 冰作为温度：空气与水的字面寒冷。

branches.en: ICE AS FEELING: a manner frozen toward other people.
branches.cn: 冰作为情感：对他人冻结的态度。

branches.en: ICE AS MEASURE AND APPEARANCE: the slowest pace, and an acid that looks like ice.
branches.cn: 冰作为尺度与外观：最慢的速度，以及看起来像冰的酸。

intro.en: Glacial is glaci- plus the Latin adjective suffix -alis, reduced to -al in English. It is the adjective member of the glacies family.
intro.cn: glacial 由 glaci- 加拉丁形容词后缀 -alis 构成，英语中缩为 -al。它是 glacies 词族的形容词成员。

latinIntro.en: Latin glacies yields the whole ice family: glacier, glacial, glaciate, glaciation, glaciology. All keep the sense of ice or freezing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 glacies 衍生整个冰词族：glacier、glacial、glaciate、glaciation、glaciology，全部保留冰或冻结之义。

items.example: Glacial, fluvial and rural share the pattern.

items.meaning: glacial cover or a glacial period
items.exampleCN: 冰川作用留下散落的巨砾。

items.example: The last glacial period ended long ago.
items.exampleCN: 最后一次冰期早已结束。

items.meaning: concentrated acetic acid that looks like ice
items.example: Glacial acetic acid must be handled carefully.

definition_en: a large mass of ice that forms on land and moves slowly under its own weight
core_image: 一条巨大的冰舌从山谷深处推出来，底部磨着岩石，末端滴着融水
scene: 山谷深处，一条灰白色的冰舌缓慢推出来，末端不断滴下融水。The glacier has ground the valley walls smooth.

senses.title: A valley glacier
senses.titleCN: 山谷冰川：沿山谷下行的冰体
senses.definition: a mass of ice confined to a valley and flowing down it
senses.definitionCN: 被限制在山谷中并向下流动的冰体
senses.example: The glacier has ground the valley walls smooth.
senses.exampleCN: 这条冰川把谷壁磨得光滑。
senses.why: glacier names a body of ice that behaves like a very slow river: it is confined by its valley and flows in one direction.
senses.whyCN: glacier 命名一种行为像极慢河流的冰体：它被山谷约束，只朝一个方向流动。

senses.title: A continental glacier
senses.titleCN: 大陆冰川：覆盖大片陆地的冰体
senses.definition: an ice mass that spreads outward over a continent rather than down a valley
senses.definitionCN: 在陆地上向外摊开、而非沿谷下行的巨大冰体
senses.example: A continental glacier once covered the northern plains.
senses.exampleCN: 一块大陆冰川曾经覆盖北方平原。
senses.why: the same noun covers both sizes, because valley ice and continental ice share the defining behaviour of spreading under their own weight.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词覆盖两种尺度，因为谷冰川与大陆冰川共享「靠自身重量向外摊开」这一界定行为。

senses.title: The ice mass itself
senses.titleCN: 冰川体量：作为一大块冰
senses.definition: the body of ice considered as a volume, with depth and mass
senses.definitionCN: 把冰体视为有厚度与质量的体积
senses.example: The glacier is hundreds of metres thick at its centre.
senses.exampleCN: 这条冰川中心处厚达数百米。
senses.why: once the mass is measured, the word names a volume with depth, not only a moving stream.
senses.whyCN: 一旦对冰体进行测量，这个词就命名一个有厚度的体积，而不只是流动的冰河。

senses.title: The slow flow of ice
senses.titleCN: 冰川流动：冰的缓慢运动
senses.definition: the slow downhill movement of ice by internal deformation and sliding
senses.definitionCN: 冰因内部变形与底部滑动而缓慢下移
senses.example: The glacier moves about a metre a day in summer.
senses.exampleCN: 夏天这条冰川每天大约移动一米。
senses.why: the defining behaviour is motion; without flow the same ice would be a snowfield, so the flow sense is central.
senses.whyCN: 界定性行为是运动；若不流动，同样的冰只是雪原，因此「流动」这一义是核心。

senses.title: The tongue or terminus
senses.definition: the lower end of a glacier, where it reaches a valley floor or a lake
senses.definitionCN: 冰川的下端，抵达谷底或湖泊之处
senses.example: The glacier tongue ends in a milky lake.
senses.exampleCN: 冰舌终止在一个乳白色的湖里。
senses.why: the terminus is where the glacier becomes visible as an edge, so the word names that projecting end.
senses.whyCN: 末端是冰川作为边缘显现之处，因此这个词命名伸出的那一端。

senses.title: An ancient glacier
senses.titleCN: 古冰川：更新世留下的冰体与遗迹
senses.definition: a glacier of an earlier geological period, known from its deposits and landforms
senses.definitionCN: 更早地质时期的冰川，由其沉积与地貌得知
senses.example: Pleistocene glaciers carved the deep fjords.
senses.exampleCN: 更新世的冰川刻出了深峡湾。
senses.why: geology reads present landforms as the work of past ice, so the word extends backward in time.
senses.whyCN: 地质学把现存地貌读作过去冰体的作品，于是这个词向时间深处延伸。

senses.title: Glacier meltwater as a resource
senses.titleCN: 冰川融水：作为水源的冰
senses.definition: the water released by a glacier, treated as a seasonal or long-term supply
senses.definitionCN: 冰川释放的水，被视为季节性或长期水源
senses.example: Farmers below depend on glacier melt in the dry months.
senses.exampleCN: 下游农民在旱月依赖冰川融水。
senses.why: meltwater is the glacier entering the water cycle, so the same noun names a water supply.
senses.whyCN: 融水是冰川进入水循环的方式，因此同一名词也命名一种水源。

senses.title: A slow unstoppable mass
senses.titleCN: 比喻：缓慢而不可阻挡的巨大力量
senses.definition: anything enormous that advances very slowly and cannot be reversed easily
senses.definitionCN: 任何巨大、推进极慢且难以逆转的事物
senses.example: A glacier of paperwork moved through the ministry.
senses.exampleCN: 一大堆文书像冰川一样在部里缓慢移动。
senses.why: the metaphor borrows two features at once: immense mass and almost invisible speed.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻同时借用了两个特征：巨大的体量与几乎看不见的速度。

intro.en: Glacier came into English from French glacier, from a Savoy dialect form of Latin glacies 'ice'. The Latin noun is the base of glacial and glaciation as well. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: glacier 经法语 glacier 进入英语，出自拉丁 glacies「冰」的萨瓦方言形式。这个拉丁名词也是 glacial 与 glaciation 的词基。年代均为约数。

items.en: Glacies meant ice, and was used of ice on water and of hard frost. Its deeper origin is often reconstructed as a root meaning cold, but the reconstruction is not universally accepted.
items.cn: glacies 意为冰，用于水面结冰与严霜。其更深来源常被重构为表示「寒冷」的词根，但这一重构未被普遍接受。

items.en: In the western Alps, speakers used a descendant of glacies for the ice rivers of the mountains; French glacier and Italian ghiacciaio both continue this local use.
items.cn: 在西阿尔卑斯山区，人们用 glacies 的后代指山中的冰河；法语 glacier 与意大利语 ghiacciaio 都延续这一地方用法。

items.en: English adopted glacier in the eighteenth century, when Alpine travel and natural history became fashionable; earlier writers used the French spelling.
items.cn: 英语在 18 世纪吸收 glacier，当时阿尔卑斯旅行与博物学成为风尚；更早的作者仍用法语拼写。

items.en: In the nineteenth century Agassiz and others argued that glaciers had once covered much of Europe, and glacier became a key term of geology.
items.cn: 19 世纪阿加西等人主张冰川曾经覆盖欧洲大部，glacier 成为地质学的关键术语。

items.en: In the twentieth and twenty-first centuries glacier retreat becomes a measurable indicator of warming, and glacier mass balance a standard quantity.
items.cn: 在 20 与 21 世纪，冰川退缩成为可测量的变暖指标，冰川质量平衡成为标准量。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-Latin root of glacies is reconstructed rather than attested, and the first English date varies by a few decades between references.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根存疑）：glacies 在拉丁语之前的词根属重构而非实证，英语首见年代各家著录相差数十年。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound like glacier but are not ice; group two holds the other terms for bodies of ice.
note.cn: 第一组是形音近似却与冰无关的词；第二组是其他冰体的术语。

entries.definition: A person who fits glass into windows; the ending is -ier, not -ier of glacier, and the root is glass.
entries.definitionCN: 安装窗玻璃的工人；词尾与 glacier 相似，但词根是 glass。

entries.definition: A French borrowing meaning iced or candied, used of fruit and leather; it is not a glacier.
entries.definitionCN: 借自法语，意为加冰的或糖渍的，用于水果与皮革；与冰川无关。

entries.definition: A gentle slope in fortification or geology; it looks like glacier but has a different ending.
entries.definitionCN: 防御工事或地质学中的缓坡；形似 glacier，词尾不同。

entries.definition: A grey-green or bluish-green surface, as on some leaves; it only sounds similar.
entries.definitionCN: 灰绿或蓝绿色表面，如某些叶片；只是读音相近。

entries.definition: A mass of ice covering a whole region and spreading outward; larger than a valley glacier.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖整个区域并向外摊开的冰体；比山谷冰川更大。

entries.definition: A dome of ice over a summit or polar area, smaller than an ice sheet.
entries.definitionCN: 覆盖山顶或极地区域的穹状冰体，小于冰盖。

entries.definition: A rapidly moving corridor within an ice sheet, behaving like a river of ice.
entries.definitionCN: 冰盖内部快速流动的走廊，行为像一条冰河。

entries.definition: A floating chunk of ice that has broken off a glacier or ice shelf.
entries.definitionCN: 从冰川或冰架断裂、漂浮的冰块。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real roots, real relatives and real collocations, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的词根、同族词与固定搭配，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: glacier and glacial share the Latin base glacies 'ice'; the noun ends in -ier, the adjective in -al.
normal.cn: glacier 与 glacial 共享拉丁词基 glacies「冰」；名词以 -ier 结尾，形容词以 -al 结尾。

normal.en: A glacier is a river of ice: confined, flowing, and ending in a tongue.
normal.cn: 冰川是一条冰之河：被约束、会流动、以冰舌收尾。

normal.en: Glacier retreat means the terminus moves uphill, not that the ice flows backwards.
normal.cn: 冰川退缩指末端向高处移动，而不是冰倒着流。

normal.en: Iceberg is the piece that breaks off; glacier is the mass it broke from.
normal.cn: iceberg 是断下来的那块，glacier 是它断自的那一整块。

normal.en: Glaciology, glaciologist and glaciation all keep the same glaci- stem.
normal.cn: glaciology、glaciologist、glaciation 都保留同一个 glaci- 词干。

abstract.en: A glacier is water that decided to move so slowly that stone had time to change.
abstract.cn: 冰川是水决定慢到让石头有时间改变。

abstract.en: Institutions can be glaciers: enormous, slow, and able to carve valleys before anyone notices.
abstract.cn: 机构也可能是冰川：庞大、缓慢，能在无人注意时刻出山谷。

abstract.en: A glacier is a library of old air, written in layers of snow.
abstract.cn: 冰川是一座旧空气的图书馆，以雪层写就。

examples.en: The glacier has retreated two kilometres in fifty years.
examples.cn: 这条冰川在五十年里退缩了两公里。

examples.en: Meltwater from the glacier feeds the valley's rivers.
examples.cn: 冰川融水供养着山谷里的河流。

examples.en: Debris carried by the glacier forms a long moraine.
examples.cn: 冰川搬运的岩屑形成一道长长的冰碛。

dict_mnemonic.text: glacier 来自拉丁 glacies（冰）：一条会流动的冰河；glacial 是它的形容词，glaciation 是它做过的事，glaciology 是研究它。

root: 经法语 glacier 上溯拉丁 glacies「冰」；同族词包括 glacial、glaciation、glaciology。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of glacier. The physical mass yields the rest: its size, its movement, its end, its ancient forms, its water, and finally its use as an image of slow power.
sensesIntro.cn: glacier 的八个义项。物理冰体衍生其余各义：体量、运动、末端、古代形态、融水，最后是「缓慢巨力」的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white river of ice pushing down a valley, grinding the walls as it goes.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条白色的冰之河沿谷下行，边走边磨蚀谷壁。

branches.en: TWO SCALES: ice confined to a valley, then ice spreading over a continent.
branches.cn: 两种尺度：先是困在谷中的冰，再是铺满大陆的冰。

branches.en: MASS AND MOTION: a thick body, then the slow flow that makes it a glacier rather than a snowfield.
branches.cn: 体量与运动：先是有厚度的冰体，再是使它成为冰川而非雪原的缓慢流动。

branches.en: THE END: the tongue, where ice meets water and turns into melt.
branches.cn: 末端：冰舌处冰与水相接并化为融水。

branches.en: DEEP TIME: the same mass read in the landforms it left behind.
branches.cn: 深时：从留下的地貌读出同一冰体。

branches.en: RESOURCE AND IMAGE: meltwater as supply, then any slow unstoppable mass.
branches.cn: 资源与意象：先是作为水源的融水，再是任何缓慢而不可阻挡的巨物。

intro.en: Glacier is a borrowing, not an English derivation: it keeps the French noun ending, while its Latin base glacies supplies the adjective and the scientific family.
intro.cn: glacier 是借词而非英语派生词：它保留法语名词词尾，其拉丁词基 glacies 则供应形容词与科学词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin glacies yields glacier, glacial, glaciate, glaciation, glaciology and glaciologist. The family is one of the most regular in earth science.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 glacies 衍生 glacier、glacial、glaciate、glaciation、glaciology、glaciologist。这个词族在地球科学中最为规整。

items.exampleCN: 冰冷的寒风从山峰吹来。

items.example: The glacier fills the upper valley.
Glacial ice is blue under compression.
items.exampleCN: 受挤压的冰川冰呈蓝色。
这片高原两次受到冰川作用。

items.exampleCN: 一位冰川学家测量了冰的厚度。

items.example: The glacier tongue reaches the lake.

definition_en: a very brief look, to see briefly, or a short understanding
core_image: 人群中一闪而过的熟悉面孔
scene: 他透过人群瞥见了她。He caught a glimpse of her through the crowd.
sceneCN: 这里 glimpse 是「一瞥」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他透过人群瞥见了她。

senses.title: A very brief look
senses.definition: a quick and incomplete view of something
senses.definitionCN: 短暂而不完整地看到某物
senses.example: He caught a glimpse of her through the crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 他透过人群瞥见了她。
senses.why: The noun names a view too short to be complete.
senses.whyCN: 名词命名一个短到来不及完整的视野。

senses.title: To see briefly
senses.definition: to see something for only a moment
senses.definitionCN: 只在刹那间看到某物
senses.example: She glimpsed a fox at the edge of the wood.
senses.exampleCN: 她瞥见树林边有一只狐狸。
senses.why: The verb turns the brief sight into an act.
senses.whyCN: 动词把短暂看见变成动作。

senses.title: A short understanding
senses.definition: a brief experience that shows you something
senses.definitionCN: 让人窥见某事的短暂体验
senses.example: The visit gave us a glimpse of village life.
senses.exampleCN: 这次访问让我们窥见了乡村生活。
senses.why: Seeing a little of a thing is also understanding a little.
senses.whyCN: 看到事物的一小部分，也就是理解了一小部分。

intro.en: Glimpse began as a faint shining, then a flash of sight.
intro.cn: glimpse 最初指微弱的光，后来指目光的一闪。

items.en: Glim meant a brightness or a glow.
items.cn: glim 意为光亮或微光。

items.cn: glimsen 意为微微发亮。

items.cn: 这个词开始表示视觉上的一闪。

items.en: A glimpse of truth extended it to understanding.

normal.en: He glimpsed at the letter and put it down.

abstract.en: A glimpse is enough to change what we believe.
abstract.cn: 一瞥，足以改变我们所相信的东西。

abstract.en: What we glimpse, we remember longer than what we study.
abstract.cn: 瞥见的东西，比攻读的东西记得更久。

abstract.en: Every great discovery begins with a glimpse.

branches.cn: 一张熟悉的脸在两个陌生人之间一闪而过。

branches.en: A fox slips into the trees.
branches.cn: 一只狐狸溜进树丛。

branches.en: A doorway opens on another way of life.
branches.cn: 一扇门透出另一种生活。

branches.en: The brief sight and the act of seeing are one moment.

definition_en: a narrow steep valley; the throat; to eat greedily; a blockage of ice in a river; a feeling of disgust
core_image: 两壁夹得极近的一条深缝，中间只容一条水线通过
scene: 两壁几乎贴在一起，河在下方发出很响的水声。The gorge narrows until the two walls almost touch.
sceneCN: 此处指「两壁陡直、宽度极小的峡谷」（第 1 个义项：窄到几乎只剩一条水道的深谷）；句意为这条峡谷越收越窄，直到两壁几乎相贴。图中可辨识物件：几乎相接的岩壁、下方湍急的水线、回声、狭窄的天空。

pos.zh: 峡谷；咽喉；作呕感；阻塞物（如冰塞）
狼吞虎咽地吃；塞满；在石料上开凹槽

derivatives.zh: 华丽的；极美的（与本词关系不确定）

senses.title: A narrow steep valley
senses.definition: a narrow valley with steep rocky sides, usually with a river at the bottom
senses.definitionCN: 两侧陡峭、底部常有河流的狭窄山谷
senses.example: The gorge narrows until the two walls almost touch.
senses.exampleCN: 这条峡谷越收越窄，直到两壁几乎相贴。
senses.why: The word first meant throat; a landscape that squeezes tight like a throat borrows the name.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指咽喉；像咽喉一样收得极紧的地形就借用了这个名字。

senses.title: The throat
senses.definition: the passage at the back of the mouth, in older or medical-style use
senses.definitionCN: 口腔后部的通道，用于较古或医学风格的表述
senses.example: Cold water eased the heat in his gorge.
senses.exampleCN: 凉水缓解了他咽喉里的燥热。
senses.why: The body part is the oldest sense: a narrow tube through which everything swallowed must pass.
senses.whyCN: 身体部位是最早的义项：一根狭窄的管子，所有吞下的东西都必须经过。

senses.title: To eat greedily
senses.definition: to eat large amounts quickly and without restraint
senses.definitionCN: 快速而无节制地吃下大量食物
senses.example: The children gorged on cake at the party.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们在聚会上猛吃蛋糕。
senses.why: Stuffing the throat to its limit turns the body-part noun into a verb of overfilling.
senses.whyCN: 把咽喉塞到极限，就把这个身体部位名词变成了「塞满」的动词。

senses.title: To fill something to excess
senses.definition: to fill a space or a person beyond what is needed
senses.definitionCN: 把空间或人填到超出所需
senses.example: Rain had gorged the ditches along the road.
senses.exampleCN: 雨水把路边的沟渠灌得满满的。
senses.why: The throat image extends to any channel that can be packed full and stop flowing.
senses.whyCN: 咽喉意象扩展到任何能被塞满并停止流动的通道。

senses.title: An ice blockage in a river
senses.definition: a mass of ice that blocks a narrow river channel and can cause flooding
senses.definitionCN: 堵塞狭窄河道、可能引发洪水的冰块堆积
senses.example: An ice gorge formed where the river bends.
senses.exampleCN: 河流转弯处形成了一道冰塞。
senses.why: A narrow channel plus a total blockage reproduces the throat that cannot pass anything.
senses.whyCN: 狭窄通道加上彻底堵塞，正好复制了什么都通不过的咽喉。

senses.title: A feeling of disgust
senses.definition: a rising feeling of nausea or strong dislike
senses.definitionCN: 上涌的恶心感或强烈厌恶
senses.example: The sight made his gorge rise.
senses.exampleCN: 那景象让他一阵作呕。
senses.why: Disgust is felt in the throat; the body-part noun names the physical sensation itself.
senses.whyCN: 厌恶感在咽喉处被感觉到；这个身体部位名词就直接命名了那种生理感受。

senses.title: A hollow moulding in stone
senses.definition: a concave curved moulding cut into stone or wood
senses.definitionCN: 在石材或木材上切出的凹圆线脚
senses.example: The mason cut a gorge along the base of the column.
senses.exampleCN: 石匠在柱基上切出一道凹圆线脚。
senses.why: A concave groove is a throat in the material: narrow, deep and hollowed out.
senses.whyCN: 凹形沟槽就是材料上的咽喉：窄、深、被掏空。

senses.title: To cut a groove into stone
senses.definition: to channel or hollow out a edge of stone or wood
senses.definitionCN: 在石材或木材的边缘开槽或掏空
senses.example: Workers gorged the edge before fitting the panel.
senses.exampleCN: 工人在安装面板前先给边缘开槽。
senses.why: The noun became a verb of making the shape, just as many tool and form words do.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为「造出该形状」的动词，许多工具词与形状词都这样变化。

intro.en: Gorge came from Old French for 'throat' and goes back to Late Latin gurga, probably connected with Latin gurges 'whirlpool'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: gorge 来自古法语「咽喉」，上溯至晚期拉丁 gurga，可能与拉丁 gurges「漩涡」有关。年代均为约数。

items.en: Late Latin gurga meant 'throat'; it is usually taken as a variant of Latin gurges 'whirlpool, gullet', though the two forms are not fully explained.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁 gurga 意为「咽喉」；通常被视为拉丁 gurges「漩涡、食道」的变体，但两种形式之间的关系并未完全说清。

items.en: Latin gurges, gurgitis named a swirling mass of water and, by transfer, the throat; the link is the idea of a channel that draws things down.
items.cn: 拉丁 gurges、gurgitis 指旋转的水体，又转指咽喉；联系在于「把东西往下吸的通道」这一意象。

items.en: Old French gorge meant 'throat, neck, bosom' and also 'a narrow pass'; both the body sense and the landscape sense already coexisted.
items.cn: 古法语 gorge 指「咽喉、颈、胸前」，也指「狭窄通道」；身体义与地貌义当时已经并存。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the fourteenth century; the 'narrow valley' sense developed from the image of a pass that squeezes like a throat.
items.cn: 英语在 14 世纪借入这个词；「窄谷」义由「像咽喉一样收紧的通道」这一意象发展而来。

items.en: The verb 'to eat greedily' and the idiom 'make one's gorge rise' both grow from the throat sense in the later Middle Ages.
items.cn: 动词「贪婪地吃」与习语「令人作呕」都从中古英语后期的咽喉义生长出来。

items.en: Source uncertain (root): the pre-Latin origin of gurges is debated, and no single Indo-European form is agreed; the dates given are approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根）：gurges 在拉丁语之前的来源有争议，没有公认的单一印欧形式；所给年代为约数。

note.en: The first group holds words that look or sound like gorge; the second holds words for narrow valleys and throats.
note.cn: 第一组是形近或音近的词；第二组是表示窄谷与咽喉的词。

entries.definition: Extremely beautiful or fine; it may go back to Old French gorgias, of uncertain link to gorge, so it is not used here as a derivative of the valley sense.
entries.definitionCN: 极美的、华丽的；可能来自古法语 gorgias，与 gorge 的关联不确定，因此这里不把它当作山谷义的派生词。

entries.definition: To cut or scoop out with a tool; the vowel is /aʊ/, not /ɔː/.
entries.definitionCN: 用工具凿出或挖出；元音是 /aʊ/ 而非 /ɔː/。

entries.definition: A spiny yellow-flowered shrub; it ends in -se and has nothing to do with valleys.
entries.definitionCN: 一种带刺、开黄花的灌木；以 -se 结尾，与山谷无关。

entries.definition: The plural of the noun or the third person of the verb; the -s marks grammar, not a new word.
entries.definitionCN: 名词复数或动词第三人称；-s 标记语法，不是新词。

entries.definition: A deep valley with steep walls, often in dry country; it is usually wider than a gorge and more strongly associated with river cutting.
entries.definitionCN: 常位于干旱地区的深陡峡谷；通常比 gorge 宽，也更强调河流切割。

entries.definition: A small deep valley cut by water; it is much smaller than a gorge and often has soil rather than rock walls.
entries.definitionCN: 由水切出的小深谷；比 gorge 小得多，壁多为土而非岩石。

entries.definition: A deep gap with vertical sides; it stresses the drop and the emptiness rather than a passable channel.
entries.definitionCN: 两侧垂直的深裂口；强调落差与空洞，而非可通行的通道。

entries.definition: The ordinary English word for the passage at the back of the mouth; gorge is its older, more literary counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 指口腔后部通道的普通英语词；gorge 是它较古、较文学化的对应词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real throat sense, the real idioms and the real compounds.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的咽喉义、真实的习语与真实的复合词。

normal.en: The throat image runs through the whole family: narrow, deep, hard to pass.
normal.cn: 咽喉意象贯穿整个词族：窄、深、难以通过。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: narrow gorge, deep gorge, ice gorge, through the gorge.
normal.cn: 固定搭配有 narrow gorge、deep gorge、ice gorge、through the gorge。

normal.en: The idiom the gorge rises keeps the physical feeling of nausea in the throat.
normal.cn: 习语 the gorge rises 保留了恶心的生理感觉，位置就在咽喉。

normal.en: To gorge on food is to fill the throat until nothing more can pass.
normal.cn: gorge on food 就是把咽喉填满，直到再也通不过任何东西。

normal.en: Compare canyon: a canyon is wide enough to stand in; a gorge is tight enough to echo.
normal.cn: 对比 canyon：峡谷宽到可以站人；gorge 窄到会产生回声。

abstract.en: Picture a funnel squeezed so hard that only a thread of water gets through.
abstract.cn: 想象一个漏斗被夹得极紧，只有一丝水能通过。

abstract.en: Picture a meal eaten so fast that the eater never tastes it.
abstract.cn: 想象一顿饭吃得太快，吃的人根本没尝到味道。

abstract.en: Picture a river blocked by ice until the water behind it rises.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河被冰堵住，后面的水于是上涨。

examples.en: The path follows the river through a narrow gorge.
examples.cn: 这条小径沿河穿过一道狭窄的峡谷。

examples.en: He gorged himself on fruit after the long fast.
examples.cn: 长时间禁食之后，他猛吃水果。

examples.en: An ice gorge blocked the river and flooded the lower fields.
examples.cn: 一道冰塞堵住了河道，淹了下游的田地。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「割（ge）+ 只（orge）」—— 两壁像被割开，只留一条窄缝 → 峡谷；咽喉

root: 古法语 gorge「咽喉、狭窄通道」← 晚期拉丁 gurga，可能与拉丁 gurges「漩涡、食道」有关；更深词根存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all come from a throat: a narrow valley, the body passage, greedy eating, overfilling, an ice blockage, nausea, a hollow moulding and the act of cutting one.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都出自「咽喉」：窄谷、身体通道、贪婪进食、填塞过量、冰堵、恶心、凹线脚，以及开槽的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a narrow tube that everything must pass through, and that can be blocked or stuffed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根所有东西都必须通过的窄管，它会堵，也会被塞满。

branches.en: THE NARROW CHANNEL: a valley squeezed like a throat, and the act of cutting such a groove.
branches.cn: 窄通道：像咽喉一样被夹紧的谷，以及切出这种凹槽的动作。

branches.en: THE BODY: the passage itself and the nausea felt inside it.
branches.cn: 身体：通道本身，以及在通道里感到的恶心。

branches.en: STUFFING: eating fast and filling any container past its limit.
branches.cn: 塞满：快速进食，以及把任何容器填过极限。

branches.en: THE BLOCKED PASS: ice turns a narrow channel into a dam.
branches.cn: 被堵的通道：冰把窄通道变成一道坝。

branches.en: THE MATERIAL GROOVE: stone and wood repeat the hollow throat shape.
branches.cn: 材料上的槽：石材与木材重复了中空咽喉的形状。

intro.en: Gorge is a French loan with a small English family; the connection to gorgeous is uncertain and is flagged rather than assumed.
intro.cn: gorge 是法语借词，英语词族不大；它与 gorgeous 的关联不确定，此处标明而非假定。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin gurga and Latin gurges supply the likely base; the pre-Latin origin is disputed, so the deeper Indo-European layer remains a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: 晚期拉丁 gurga 与拉丁 gurges 提供可能的基底；拉丁语之前的来源有争议，更深的印欧层次仍属重构。

items.meaning: a trail running through a gorge

items.exampleCN: 大雨之后峡谷小径封闭。

definition_en: very beautiful or colourful, or extremely pleasant
core_image: 夕阳把整片天空染成金红，云层像被点燃一样层层铺开
scene: 夕阳把天空染成绚丽的橙色。The sunset turned the sky a gorgeous orange.
sceneCN: 这里 gorgeous 是「绚丽的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：夕阳把天空染成绚丽的橙色。

senses.title: Splendid in colour
senses.definition: extremely beautiful, rich, or bright in appearance
senses.definitionCN: 外观极其美丽、浓艳或明亮
senses.example: The sunset turned the sky a gorgeous orange.
senses.exampleCN: 夕阳把天空染成绚丽的橙色。
senses.why: This is the original sense of rich, showy beauty.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示浓艳、华美外观的本义。

senses.title: Extremely good
senses.definition: very pleasant or enjoyable, used in informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 非常令人愉快或享受，用于口语
senses.example: We had a gorgeous time at the beach.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在海边度过了极好的时光。
senses.why: Everyday speech stretched beauty into general praise.
senses.whyCN: 日常口语把美丽扩展为泛泛的赞美。

senses.title: Beautiful to look at
senses.definition: very attractive in appearance, often of a person
senses.definitionCN: 外貌非常吸引人，常指人
senses.example: She looked gorgeous in that dress.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿那条裙子美极了。
senses.why: People borrowed the word for striking personal beauty.
senses.whyCN: 人们借用这个词来形容动人的个人美貌。

intro.en: Gorgeous came from Old French gorgias, meaning elegant and finely dressed.
intro.cn: gorgeous 来自古法语 gorgias，意为优雅、衣着讲究。

items.en: Gorgias described a fashionable, elegant man.
items.cn: gorgias 形容时髦优雅的人。

items.en: Gorgeous entered English meaning showy and splendid.
items.cn: gorgeous 以华丽、辉煌之义进入英语。

items.en: It was used of rich colours and fine clothes.
items.cn: 它用来形容浓艳的色彩和华美的衣服。

items.en: It spread to landscapes and beautiful people.
items.cn: 它扩展到景色和美丽的人。

items.en: Informal speech made it a general word of praise.
items.cn: 口语使它成为泛泛的赞美词。

note.en: Gorgeous is compared with look-alike words and words for beauty.
note.cn: 把 gorgeous 与形近词以及表示美丽的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Gorgeous is beauty with the volume turned up.

definition_en: to rule a country or group, to control an organization, or to determine how something works

definition_zh: 治理；治理方式；治理结构；（公司、数据等领域的）治理机制
definition_en: the way an organization or society is directed and held to account, including its rules and decision-making structures
core_image: 一张长桌，代表们按程序发言、表决、记录，散会后留下的是可被追问的决定
scene: 董事会按既定程序审议预算，投完票后把异议一并记入会议记录。Governance leaves a paper trail that any outsider can follow.
sceneCN: 这里 governance 指使决定可被追问的那套治理方式（第 1 个义项：作为整体实践）；句意为治理会留下任何外部人都能追查的书面线索。

pos.zh: 治理；治理方式（不可数，指过程与机制；作可数时指某种治理安排）

derivatives.zh: 统治；支配（拉丁 gubernare「掌舵」，由操船转指操持事务）
州长；管理者（govern + -or「行事者」，由动作转指人）
政府；政体（govern + -ment「结果或机构」，由动作转指机关）
可治理的（govern + -able「可被」，由动作转指可能性）

senses.title: Direction of a society
senses.definition: the whole practice of steering public affairs, including rules, institutions and accountability
senses.definitionCN: 引导公共事务的整体实践，含规则、机构与问责
senses.example: Governance is judged by outcomes, not by org charts.
senses.exampleCN: 治理的好坏看结果，不看组织架构图。
senses.why: the suffix -ance names an activity rather than an office, so governance points at the doing of rule.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ance 指活动而非机关，因此 governance 指向统治的进行过程。

senses.title: Corporate governance
senses.definition: the system by which a company's board, managers and shareholders are balanced and held to account
senses.definitionCN: 平衡并约束董事会、管理层与股东的制度安排
senses.example: Corporate governance determines who may overrule the chief executive.
senses.exampleCN: 公司治理决定谁能否决首席执行官。
senses.why: once the word detached from the state, companies borrowed it for their own internal checks.
senses.whyCN: 这个词一旦脱离国家，公司便借它来指自身的内部制衡。

senses.title: The machinery of rules
senses.definition: the specific bodies, procedures and reporting lines through which decisions are made
senses.definitionCN: 做出决定所依的具体机构、程序与汇报线
senses.example: The treaty created a governance structure with three committees.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约建立了含三个委员会的治理结构。
senses.why: structure is what makes a practice repeatable, so governance often names the arrangement rather than the act.
senses.whyCN: 结构让实践可重复，因此 governance 常指安排而非行为。

senses.title: How public affairs are handled
senses.definition: the style and quality of public administration, whether open, lawful and responsive or not
senses.definitionCN: 公共行政的风格与品质，是否公开、依法、有回应
senses.example: Poor governance shows up first as missing records.
senses.exampleCN: 治理不佳最先表现为记录缺失。
senses.why: the word lets observers compare systems without naming a government or a party.
senses.whyCN: 这个词让观察者比较不同体制，而不必点名某个政府或政党。

senses.title: Good governance as a standard
senses.definition: a donor and policy standard combining transparency, rule of law, participation and effectiveness
senses.definitionCN: 由透明、法治、参与与效能构成的援助与政策标准
senses.example: Loans were tied to good governance benchmarks.
senses.exampleCN: 贷款与善治指标挂钩。
senses.why: aid agencies needed a measurable word that could attach to conditions, and governance filled it.
senses.whyCN: 援助机构需要一个可量化、能附条件的词，governance 正好填空。

senses.title: Global governance
senses.definition: the informal and formal arrangements by which states and bodies manage shared problems without a world state
senses.definitionCN: 各国与各机构在没有世界政府的情况下管理共同问题的正式与非正式安排
senses.example: Climate talks are a test case of global governance.
senses.exampleCN: 气候谈判是全球治理的一个试验场。
senses.why: problems cross borders while authority does not, so the word was stretched above the state.
senses.whyCN: 问题跨境而权威不跨境，于是这个词被拉到国家之上。

senses.title: Governance of data and systems
senses.definition: the rules deciding who may collect, access, change and delete an organization's information
senses.definitionCN: 决定谁能收集、访问、修改与删除组织信息的规则
senses.example: Data governance decides who may delete a customer record.
senses.exampleCN: 数据治理决定谁能删除客户记录。
senses.why: the newest extension keeps the core idea of accountable control while dropping the state entirely.
senses.whyCN: 最新引申保留了「可问责的控制」这一内核，却完全去掉了国家。

senses.title: Exercise of governing authority
senses.definition: the actual wielding of authority, as distinct from the institutions that hold it
senses.definitionCN: 权威的实际行使，区别于持有权威的机构
senses.example: Authority was clear on paper; governance in practice was improvised.
senses.exampleCN: 纸面上的权责很清楚，实际的治理却是临时应付。
senses.why: the older abstract sense survives: governance is what happens when authority is used, not merely where it sits.
senses.whyCN: 更早的抽象义仍在：治理是权威被使用时的情形，而不只是它所在的位置。

intro.en: Governance comes from Old French governer, from Latin gubernare 'to steer a ship', itself borrowed from Greek kybernan 'to steer'. The -ance suffix names the activity. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: governance 来自古法语 governer，上溯拉丁 gubernare「操船」，后者借自希腊 kybernan「掌舵」。-ance 后缀指这一活动。年代均为约数。

items.en: Kybernan meant 'to steer, pilot a ship', and its metaphorical use for guiding people is already Greek.
items.cn: kybernan 意为「掌舵、操船」，以之隐喻引导人，在希腊语中已然存在。

items.en: Latin took the verb as gubernare 'to steer, direct, rule', and gubernator named the helmsman and then a governor.
items.cn: 拉丁语取来作 gubernare「操船、指引、统治」，gubernator 既指舵手也指治理者。

items.en: Old French governer carried it into English in the thirteenth century, first as a verb of steering and directing.
items.cn: 古法语 governer 在 13 世纪把它带入英语，最初是操船与指引的动词。

items.en: Governance appeared later as the abstract noun of the act, parallel to government, which named the body rather than the doing.
items.cn: governance 较晚出现，是这一行为的抽象名词，与指机关而非行为的 government 并行。

items.en: In the late twentieth century governance spread to corporate boards, global institutions and data systems, always keeping accountability at its centre.
items.cn: 20 世纪后期 governance 扩展到公司董事会、全球机构与数据系统，始终以问责为核心。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Greek origin of kybernan is not established, and the forms proposed for it are reconstructions rather than demonstrated ancestors.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：kybernan 在希腊语之前的来源未得到证明，为其提出的形式属重构形式，而非已证的祖先。

note.en: Group one shares the govern root; group two holds near neighbours in public management.
note.cn: 第一组共享 govern 词根；第二组是公共管理领域的近义词。

entries.definition: The institutions that hold authority, formed with -ment 'result, means'; governance is the activity those institutions perform.
entries.definitionCN: 持有权威的机构，由 -ment「结果、手段」构成；governance 是这些机构所进行的活动。

entries.definition: To steer or rule directly; the noun shifts attention from the actor to the arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 直接操持或统治；名词把注意力从行动者移到安排上。

entries.definition: One who governs a province, state or institution; it names a holder of office, not a process.
entries.definitionCN: 治理一省、一州或一机构的人；指任职者，而非过程。

entries.definition: Of a governor, from the same Latin gubernator; it looks unlike govern but shares the helmsman image.
entries.definitionCN: 指州长的，同出拉丁 gubernator；形似无关，却共享舵手意象。

entries.definition: The execution of policy by staff; governance adds accountability and the rule-setting level above execution.
entries.definitionCN: 由人员执行政策；governance 另加问责与执行之上的定规层面。

entries.definition: The everyday running of an organization's work; governance concerns who may direct and how they answer for it.
entries.definitionCN: 组织日常工作的运转；governance 关注谁有权指挥以及如何为此负责。

entries.definition: The specific rules imposed on an activity; governance is the wider frame that produces and enforces them.
entries.definitionCN: 施加于某项活动的具体规则；governance 是产生并执行它们的更宽框架。

entries.definition: Responsible care of something entrusted to one, close to governance in tone but without the machinery of office.
entries.definitionCN: 对所托付之物的负责照管，语气接近 governance，但不含机关机器。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: govern + -ance: the doing of steering, not the steering body.
normal.cn: govern + -ance：掌舵这件事，而非掌舵的机构。

normal.en: Latin gubernare is a ship's helm, so governance keeps the image of a hand on the tiller.
normal.cn: 拉丁 gubernare 是船舵，因此 governance 始终带着一只手扶舵的画面。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: corporate governance, global governance, data governance.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：公司治理、全球治理、数据治理。

normal.en: The family runs govern, governor, government, governable, gubernatorial.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 govern、governor、government、governable、gubernatorial。

normal.en: Accountability is the test word: if nobody can be asked why, it is not governance.
normal.cn: 问责是试金石：若无人可被追问缘由，那就不算治理。

abstract.en: Picture a hand on a tiller while the crew argues about the course.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手扶着舵，船员们同时在争论航向。

abstract.en: Picture a meeting that ends with a minute anyone can later read.
abstract.cn: 想象一场会开完留下一份谁都能日后查阅的记录。

abstract.en: Picture a rulebook whose authors must sign each page.
abstract.cn: 想象一本规则手册，每一页都要作者签名。

examples.en: The fund tied its grants to improvements in local governance.
examples.cn: 该基金把拨款与地方治理的改善挂钩。

examples.en: Corporate governance failed long before the share price fell.
examples.cn: 公司治理在股价下跌之前很久就已失灵。

examples.en: Data governance decides who may read the archive.
examples.cn: 数据治理决定谁可以读取档案。

dict_mnemonic.text: govern（掌舵）+ ance（行为）＝ 掌舵这件事；记「船往哪开、谁在扶舵、事后谁解释」。

root: 古法语 governer ← 拉丁 gubernare「操船、治理」← 希腊 kybernan「掌舵」；kybernan 在希腊语之前的来源不确定，相关更早形式属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one hand on a tiller: steering a society, steering a company, the frame that makes steering repeatable, the quality of the steering, its policy standard, its global stretch, its newest data form, and the plain exercise of authority.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项随一只手扶舵展开：引导社会、引导公司、使引导可重复的框架、引导的品质、其政策标准、其全球延伸、其最新的数据形态，以及权威的单纯行使。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand on a tiller, a course agreed in public, and a record that lets others ask why.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手扶着舵，航向公开商定，还留下可供他人追问缘由的记录。

branches.en: THE ACT ITSELF: steering a society, and the bare wielding of authority.
branches.cn: 行为本身：引导社会，以及权威的单纯行使。

branches.en: THE COMPANY VERSION: the same helm inside a firm.
branches.cn: 公司版本：同一副舵搬进企业内部。

branches.en: THE FRAME: bodies and reporting lines make steering repeatable.
branches.cn: 框架：机构与汇报线让引导可以重复。

branches.en: QUALITY AND YARDSTICK: how well it steers, then the standard used to grade it.
branches.cn: 品质与标尺：先问掌舵好不好，再给出评分标准。

branches.en: TWO NEW DOMAINS: above the state, and inside the database.
branches.cn: 两个新领域：国家之上，以及数据库之内。

intro.en: Governance is govern plus -ance, and govern itself is a Latin borrowing ultimately from a Greek verb of steering.
intro.cn: governance 是 govern 加 -ance，而 govern 本身是源自希腊掌舵动词的拉丁借词。

latinIntro.en: Latin gubernare and gubernator give govern, governor, government and gubernatorial; the ship's helm is the shared image.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 gubernare 与 gubernator 衍生 govern、governor、government、gubernatorial；共同的意象是船舵。
